about: Excerpts of session-map's own code (server/*.mjs, identifiers lightly changed): 15 with one planted, realistic bug and 5 clean controls. bugLines are 1-based line numbers of code.split("\n"); show the code to the model numbered the same way. The model answers {"bugs": [{"line": n, "why": "..."}]}, empty when it finds none. Each bug was proven by a behaviour check that fails as written and passes once the planted line is fixed; each clean item passes the same kind of check.

items.bug: 'Today' is cut at UTC midnight instead of the owner's local midnight, so in Brazil the evening's spend after 21:00 drops out of today.
isBelow never rejects a relative path that starts with '..', so '../other/secret.txt' (or an absolute path on the same drive) is read from outside the project.
On an HTTP error the request headers, which hold "Authorization: Bearer <key>", are written to the log.
The range end is from + count, one line past the last changed line (both ends are meant to be included).
LOOPBACK_HOST_RE has no '$' anchor, so a rebinding host such as 'localhost.attacker.example' counts as local and reads the map without the token.
When sealing the key fails the error is only logged: the entry is saved without its data and saveKey still answers ok.
The call is only counted after the await, so asks made at the same time all pass the hourly check and the cap is exceeded.
Each cost is rounded to whole cents before it is added, so calls costing a fraction of a cent book US$ 0 and the daily cap is never reached.
Object.assign(DEFAULTS, ...) writes every project's settings into the shared DEFAULTS, so one project's roadmap and decisions leak into the next project loaded.
psQuote wraps values in double quotes, where PowerShell still expands $(...) and $variables, so a branch or folder name like $(calc) runs a command.
Past the limit the entries are sorted oldest first and the first ones kept, so the newest answers (even the one just stored) are dropped instead of the oldest.
The Luhn check doubles the even positions from the right (i % 2 === 0) instead of the odd ones, so real card numbers fail it and go out unmasked.
The 'longest key wins' test is reversed (key.length < best.length), so the shortest matching key wins and claude-opus-5-5 is billed at claude-opus-5's price.
return this.#apiRun(...) without await inside try: a rejected helper call escapes the catch, so answer() rejects instead of falling back to Claude.
dayKey uses getDay() (the weekday, 0-6) instead of getDate() (the day of the month), so every Saturday of a month lands on the same key.
